about: The mutation each guard in this repo must redden on. Read by
scripts/run_mutation_witness_tests.mjs (which applies each mutation to a
shadow copy of the tree and fails if the named tier stays green) and by
tests/test_mutation_witnesses.py (which checks, on every pytest run and
with no browser, that every `find` below still resolves to exactly one
place in the file it names).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A guard's witness is often coupled to an incidental
property of the app -- a viewport where the document happened to be short,
a preference that happened to be at its default, a measurement that
re-derives whatever is on screen. When the app changes CORRECTLY the
coupling breaks, the guard silently stops witnessing anything, and nothing
goes red to announce that the coverage left. Five of those were filed by
five different review sessions between 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-15, three of
them found only because a reviewer mutated the code by hand and noticed the
suite stayed green. An entry here is how that hand check becomes a standing
one.
ADDING AN ENTRY IS THE POINT -- it has to be cheaper than filing an issue.
Copy the nearest entry and change five strings. `find` is any exact,
UNIQUE snippet of the file (leading indentation included); `replace` is
the broken version; `expect_red` is the sub-check name the owning tier
PRINTS when it fails, copied verbatim off that output.
`tier` NAMES A HARNESS, not a speed. It is one of:
fast      apps/viewer/run_tests.cjs -- the VIEWER's fast tier, whose
check names live in the tests.js it loads
annotate  apps/annotate/run_tests.cjs -- the annotate app's own fast
tier, which is both the harness AND where its check names
are written. A separate word rather than a second meaning
for "fast", because they are separate harnesses with separate
name sources (added 2026-09-16, ISSUE_20260915_the_annotate_
fast_tier_cannot_own_a_mutation_witness)
browser   scripts/run_viewer_browser_tests.mjs
The tier words themselves are written in exactly two places -- `TIER_HARNESS` in
run_mutation_witness_tests.mjs and `TIERS`/`CHECK_SOURCE` in
tests/test_mutation_witnesses.py -- and paired against each other on
every pytest run. A browser entry also names the `suite`, which is passed
straight to that runner's --only filter, so one mutation costs one suite
rather than a full run of every suite; neither fast tier has suites, so
their entries carry `suite: null`. (The runner prints the count it
actually filtered down from; no number is written out here, because
nothing would keep it true.)
The mutations are DECLARED, never applied to this tree: the runner copies
everything a tier reads into tmp/mutation-witness/ and patches the copy.
`SHADOWED` in run_mutation_witness_tests.mjs is that list, and the only
place it is written down -- read it there rather than from a copy here,
which is how this line went stale once already (2026-09-16).
ONE THING AN ENTRY CANNOT DECLARE: a mutation that breaks the page itself
rather than one behaviour -- removing the popover's room cap, say -- stops
a later hover or wait from ever completing and takes its whole suite down
as an ERROR. That red is real, and louder than a failed assertion, but it
carries no check name for the runner to attribute, so it is reported as a
miss. Narrow the mutation until it fails an assertion, or leave that guard
to the hand check it already survives.

mutations.contract: Hover chrome is out of flow: an open card is placed in the window's frame, not the document's, so it disturbs no layout and follows its trigger at any scroll.
mutations.note: The room cap made the original witness unreachable -- the card is now always wholly inside the window, and at scrollY 0 document and viewport coordinates coincide. The witness had to move to a scrolled document (CARD_SCROLL_VIEWPORT).
mutations.find: display: none; position: fixed; z-index: 20; width: 540px;
mutations.replace: display: none; position: absolute; z-index: 20; width: 540px;
mutations.expect_red: an open card is placed in the WINDOW's frame, not the document's — it still sits against its trigger with the page scrolled

mutations.contract: A served page with nothing published gets one plain sentence AND NOTHING ELSE -- in particular not the switch-to-Chrome advice written for the other no-adapter state, which is untrue of a hosted visitor's situation.
mutations.note: Every other sub-check on that bar looks for something ABSENT, so all of them pass while a second element rides along.
mutations.expect_red: the bar carries that one sentence and nothing else — no second element offering advice that is untrue of a hosted visitor

mutations.contract: A study that REFUSED has no chain, so clicking it leaves the walk at FULL emphasis -- nothing dimmed, every leader, the whole table. The error is the result.
mutations.note: Re-pointed by viewer_respine_whole_walk (2026-09-15): the condition used to be topology_app.js's chainable() picking a layout, and is now views/topology.js's one `marking` test, which gates the dimming, the leader subset and the grid subset together. The witness still has to arrive from a SUMMING study -- reached from the deselected walk, a refusal and no selection at all draw the same page, which is why this shipped green in all three tiers.
mutations.expect_red: a refusing study leaves the walk exactly as it was rather than emphasizing a chain it has not got

mutations.contract: Selecting a study never changes what is ON SCREEN: the rails are always VA.spineRight(topoProj.layout), so every node, edge, rail and link of the document survives the selection. The old behaviour swapped in study.layout, which is what Jeff read as a defect.
mutations.note: Declared in review of viewer_respine_whole_walk (2026-09-15). The handoff's headline deliverable, and its single undo is this one expression -- the same shape as viewer_dag_spine_layout's `VA.spineRight` call, which shipped green in all three tiers when its CALL was deleted. Measured by hand here: the mutation reddens three fast-tier checks. Entered because the tactical lesson carried no mutation list for the three emphasis contracts.
mutations.replace: var layout = VA.spineRight(study && study.layout ? study.layout : topoProj.layout);
mutations.expect_red: selecting a study never hides a node or an edge: the DAG is the whole walk before and after, whatever the study is

mutations.contract: With a study selected the merged-row grid holds exactly the chain's edges: VA.gridPlan's `focus.edges` filter drops every walk row outside the chain.
mutations.note: Declared in review of viewer_respine_whole_walk (2026-09-15), the second of the three emphasis contracts. This is the half of the deliverable that is NOT visible on the rails, so a reader comparing screenshots cannot see it go; two fast-tier plan-level checks and one render-level check redden on the mutation.
mutations.expect_red: selecting a study dims the non-members, numbers the chain and drops the grid to the chain's own rows

mutations.contract: A leader is drawn only where it points at a CHAIN node. The absence of a line -- not a faded one -- is the emphasis signal Jeff asked for first: "it should be fairly obvious that there are no leader lines pointing to certain elements".
mutations.note: Declared in review of viewer_respine_whole_walk (2026-09-15), the third of the three emphasis contracts. `rail__leader--off` was deleted with this change, so nothing in the CSS can express the old faded-leader state any more -- which means a regression here shows up as leaders to non-members at full strength, not as a fade.
mutations.expect_red: the leaders run to the chain and nowhere else, and every one of them lands on a seam one of its OWN edges bounds

mutations.contract: The row-density toggle actually changes the row pitch, to VA.ROW_DENSITIES' own compact number.
mutations.note: The correspondence check beside it re-derives both leader ends from the live DOM, so it holds at either density and anchors nothing on its own. The mutation is the toggle quietly becoming a no-op.
mutations.expect_red: the density toggle really took — the rows are at ROW_DENSITIES' compact pitch, and were at its comfortable one before the click

mutations.contract: state.leaderStyle is a display preference, so selectTopology() never resets it -- the claim apps/viewer/topology_app.js and apps/viewer/README.md both make in prose.
mutations.note: The suite used to toggle the style back to its jogged default BEFORE its only topology switch, where a reset and a non-reset are indistinguishable. The sibling preference (jogZoneScale) was covered all along.
mutations.expect_red: [real] switching topology keeps the leader STYLE too

mutations.contract: state.rowDensity is a display preference, so selectTopology() never resets it -- the precedent the other three preferences' comments all invoke.
mutations.note: Found chasing that issue's closing question -- whether the OLDER preferences had the same hole. They did: this reddened nothing in any tier on 2026-09-15, for the same reason leaderStyle did not, and is entered beside the two below it as one contract in three parts.
mutations.expect_red: [real] switching topology keeps the density, the length mode and the value-only rows as well

mutations.contract: state.edgeLengthMode is a display preference, so selectTopology() never resets it.
mutations.note: The sibling of the entry above; see its note.
mutations.expect_red: [real] switching topology keeps the density, the length mode and the value-only rows as well

mutations.contract: state.edgeValueOnly is a display preference, so selectTopology() never resets it.
mutations.note: The sibling of the two entries above; see the first one's note.
mutations.expect_red: [real] switching topology keeps the density, the length mode and the value-only rows as well

mutations.contract: An http(s) page whose served probes fail is UNPUBLISHED, never FSA: a hosted visitor has no tolstack repo to grant, so the folder picker is not offered at all.
mutations.note: Already sound when this table was written (2026-09-15) -- entered as a standing witness, and as the fast-tier worked example this file otherwise would not have. Verified by hand in the review that filed the unpublished-banner issue. RE-POINTED at the merge into integration, 2026-09-15: afbed4e (handoff surfaces_that_state_something_false) replaced `opts.protocol !== FILE_PROTOCOL` with `!VA.isLocalPage(opts.protocol, opts.hostname)` so the annotator's loopback origin counts as local too. Same branch, same defect if it goes; the anchor check caught the rot on the first pytest run after the merge, which is the whole reason it is in pytest.
mutations.expect_red: an http page whose served probes both fail never boots FSA -- a hosted visitor has no repo to grant, so Connect folder is not offered at all

mutations.contract: views/banner.js has a branch for UNPUBLISHED at all -- the plain sentence, with no Connect folder button under it.
mutations.note: The other half of the unpublished bar, and already sound: this one pins the sentence, the entry above pins 'and nothing else'. Entered together so the pair is visible as a pair.
mutations.expect_red: a served page with nothing published states it in plain words and offers NO control -- never Connect folder, which a hosted visitor could not satisfy

mutations.contract: The detail pane's annotate-this link is gated on BOTH rules, not just the gap one: an edge with a gap to close whose part has no 3D model is offered nothing at all, because the click would land on the annotator's empty state.
mutations.note: The guard this witnesses used to name `hub` as the meshless part, so installing a hub mesh in the sibling rotorkit repo reddened it for a reason unrelated to the behaviour. It now picks every live edge with a gap to close whose part's mesh does not resolve, so the witness survives any mesh set -- measured green with 27 extra meshes installed.
mutations.expect_red: [real] every untraced edge whose part has NO mesh offers nothing at all -- not a disabled control, not an explanation

mutations.contract: The other half of the same rule: where a mesh DOES resolve the link is really offered, carrying that edge's own topology/edge/study/part identity. Withholding it everywhere would satisfy the entry above on its own.
mutations.note: Inverts the pane's mesh gate rather than blinding VA.partHasMesh, so the red comes from the pane's behaviour and not from the test's own classifier changing under it. This mutation reddens the entry above too; the runner only requires the declared check among the failures.
mutations.expect_red: [real] every untraced edge whose part HAS a mesh offers a working annotate-this link, wherever the mesh set has reached

mutations.contract: A hosted annotate page says annotating is unavailable and then shows nothing that instructs it -- no bind hint, no pickers, no parts panel, no empty 3D pane and no dev console.
mutations.note: Every sub-check that existed before this one reads the TOP BAR -- the banner sentence, the Connect button, the transport line, the origin itself and the pageerror list -- and not one of them looks below it. The banner was already honest while the page under it told the reader to click a face in a 3D view that does not exist on that origin, so a mutation that puts the workspace back leaves all six of them green (measured in review 2026-09-15: 12/18, and the six reds are exactly the six sub-checks added with this entry).
mutations.suite: annotate hosted posture (no folder grant off-machine)
mutations.expect_red: the bind instruction is gone -- it named a 3D view this origin does not have

mutations.contract: A control the hosted branch withholds is never wired either -- hiding what a reader can see while leaving a live handler behind it is a second defect, not the same one.
mutations.note: Added in REVIEW (2026-09-15), not by the handoff. Moving main()'s whole wiring block below the hosted early-return is the second half of that handoff's deliverable 1 -- the dev console was the one control that was live as well as visible -- and it shipped with no declared witness. This mutation wires the console back up INSIDE the hosted branch: withheld and live, the exact shape the move exists to make unreachable. Observed failing by hand before it was declared. The sibling entry's mutation does not redden this sub-check and this one does not redden the sibling's, which is why both are declared.
mutations.suite: annotate hosted posture (no folder grant off-machine)
mutations.expect_red: and it was never wired -- no live handler behind the withheld control

mutations.contract: A column a respine ADDS is drawn collapsed onto the OUTGOING FRAME'S LEFTMOST RAIL and unfolds out of it -- which is why rails carry no opacity of their own, and which has to hold from a transition frame as well as from a settled one.
mutations.note: The mutation is the pre-2026-09-15 behaviour exactly: clamp the drawn column index at 0 rather than at the outgoing frame's own leftmost index. A SETTLED outgoing frame always has a rail at drawn 0, so every guard that starts from one stays green; the witness has to interrupt a transition at e = 0.5, where the spine sits at drawn 4.5 with nothing to its left.
mutations.expect_red: a respine interrupting a respine unfolds out of a rail the frame it interrupted really drew — not out of drawn column 0, which a frame caught mid-unfold has nothing on

mutations.contract: A link belongs to a PAIR of columns and cannot be in the store's keyed alpha map, so it carries an opacity of its own: a link a respine adds between two columns BOTH serialisations have fades in instead of appearing whole on rails that never move.
mutations.note: Unobservable in the committed corpus and deliberately witnessed synthetically: all 21 study chains are linear (columns 1, links []), so every link a respine adds today arrives on a column the respine also adds and the unfold covers it. The mutation is the pre-fix behaviour -- every drawn link opaque at every e.
mutations.expect_red: a link a respine ADDS between two columns BOTH serialisations have fades in — the column unfold cannot cover it, because neither column is one the transition adds

mutations.contract: The link opacity the geometry computes reaches the DOM: railsSvg draws each fan-out and loop closure through fadeLink, so a link the respine adds wears its own inline opacity and a settled frame wears none.
mutations.note: The other half of a-link-a-respine-adds-fades-in: that entry breaks the number, this one breaks the wiring. VA.linkOpacity staying correct while the view stops reading it is the exact shape of a guard that quietly witnesses nothing.
mutations.find:
svg.appendChild(fadeLink(VA.svg("path",
        "rail__link rail__link--" + link.kind, { d: link.d }), link.key));
mutations.expect_red: the rendered frame carries a link's fade on the drawn path, and a settled frame carries none

mutations.contract: .tv__rails { position: sticky; left: 0 } holds the DAG against the pane's VISIBLE left edge, so a reader who scrolls the grid sideways keeps their rails beside the rows those rails align with.
mutations.note: Browser tier only, and it has to be: the DOM shim has no layout to scroll. Every other respine check in either tier runs at scrollLeft 0, where the claim holds of a pane with no sticky at all -- which is why testRespine's scrolled arm sets scrollLeft before measuring. The arm also pins the LIMIT (the sticky runs out of containing block past paneWidth - dagWidth) in a second sub-check, which the issue above tracks.
mutations.find: flex: none; display: block; position: sticky; left: 0; z-index: 1;
mutations.replace: flex: none; display: block; position: static; left: 0; z-index: 1;
mutations.expect_red: [real] scrolled sideways, the DAG stays pinned to the pane's VISIBLE left edge — `.tv__rails` is sticky, which is what keeps a scrolled reader's rails beside their own rows

mutations.contract: Every nav click repaints the page, whatever the worksheet read does: a rejected read lands in the banner and the rail's highlight still moves to the row that was clicked.
mutations.note: The mutation is the bug Jeff reported on 2026-09-15 ("the page gets wedged on that item and can't unstick unless you do a page refresh") -- one missing rejection handler. Only the rows whose subject declares a worksheet_file read anything, so the witness needs the REAL projection. That was 10 of the surviving rows before this handoff (pitch_system, its 7 studies, the 2 thermal stacks); the worksheet fallback added in the same handoff makes it 26 of 28, and the suite prints the pair it actually exercised so a future drop shows up as a small number rather than a green run.
mutations.suite: no nav click wedges the page
mutations.expect_red: no click leaves the page wedged: every row still moves the rail's highlight when the worksheet read fails

mutations.contract: The grid's merged component cell, the preview pane's heading, a hover card's heading and an interface's side list all print a part's NAME. An id is a deep-link handle and is rendered nowhere a reader reads -- Jeff, 2026-09-15: "2nd line bolt_nas6403u11d appears to be some type of internal id that is meaningless to user".
mutations.note: Swaps the fallback order rather than deleting the name, so a part WITH a name renders its id and a part without one is unaffected -- which is the exact defect, not a crash. Reddens 17 tests; the declared one is the fixture-tier statement of the rule, so it witnesses without a projection on disk. Reasoning and the measurements: docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_viewer_component_names_and_reference_copy.md.
mutations.expect_red: the component label is the part's own name, and an id is what it is keyed by -- never what is printed

mutations.contract: The "open the PDF" link renders only on an origin that can service a file: navigation. Chrome refuses every navigation from an http(s) page to a file: URL, so on a served page the click did nothing at all (Jeff, 2026-09-15) -- and a control that does nothing must be absent, not explained.
mutations.note: Reverts the one call to the pure URL builder, which is exactly the pre-fix code. VA.fileUrl is deliberately still pure and still exported, so this mutation is the real regression rather than a synthetic one. Reasoning and the measurements: docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_viewer_component_names_and_reference_copy.md.
mutations.expect_red: a local-file link renders only where the origin can follow it

mutations.contract: No surface renders an absolute workstation path. It was the fallback for a link that could not navigate; the link now renders only where it works, so the fallback has nothing to fall back from -- Jeff, 2026-09-15: "full workstation file paths -- never rendered when the link works".
mutations.note: Puts the path line back where it used to be, in the ONE shared crop builder, so the mutation reaches all four crop surfaces at once. The declared check is the fixture-tier banned-string walk; the [real] walk over every live topology reddens too. Reasoning and the measurements: docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_viewer_component_names_and_reference_copy.md.
mutations.expect_red: no rendered topology surface prints an internal id, a field name, a checksum or a workstation path

mutations.contract: The preview pane is RIGHT of its divider, so dragging left widens it. The sign lives in the pure layer (VA.paneWidthAfterDrag) precisely because getting it backwards is the likeliest mistake in the feature and the app shell cannot be checked without a pointer.
mutations.note: Flips the sign only. The clamp still holds, so a mutated build still 'works' -- it resizes the wrong way, which is the defect a reader would report and the one a green suite must not allow. Reasoning and the measurements: docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_viewer_component_names_and_reference_copy.md.
mutations.expect_red: the preview pane's width clamps, and a drag on its divider widens it by moving LEFT

mutations.contract: A crop says where on it to look: every surface that shows a crop draws the crop's own `highlights[]` over the picture, in the same frame as the ``. A crop that widened and marked nothing is worse than the tight strip it replaced, and it looks perfectly fine in a screenshot.
mutations.note: Declared in review 2026-09-16 (REVIEW_20260915_viewer_reference_crops_in_context), from a hand mutation that did redden. Removes the overlay loop from the ONE shared figure builder, so it reaches all four crop surfaces at once; four fast-tier sub-checks go red, the named one first. The four OTHER wires of this deliverable that stayed green under mutation could not be declared here, because no check reddens on them -- see ISSUE_20260916_the_crop_overlays_wiring_is_unwitnessed_in_every_tier.md.
mutations.expect_red: a datasheet crop draws its used cell as a box positioned in PERCENTAGES of the image

mutations.contract: The annotate app's no-projection banner is PLAIN WORDS: it says where the projection is built and stops. Jeff's standing rule across every web surface in this workspace -- a terminal command is never rendered for a reader to copy.
mutations.note: The first entry on the `annotate` tier word (2026-09-16). It restores the exact shape the defect had -- "Build it: " with an interpreter and a script path concatenated on (ISSUE_20260915_annotate_banner_renders_a_terminal_command_for_the_user_to_copy) -- so the guard is checked against the sentence it was written for rather than a synthetic one.
mutations.find:
"No topology projection in the connected folder. It is built in the " +
    "tolerance-stack repository, not from this page.";
mutations.replace:
"No topology projection in the connected folder. Build it: " +
    "venv-win/Scripts/python.exe scripts/build_topology_projection.py";
mutations.expect_red: the no-projection banner is plain words, with nothing to paste

mutations.contract: The copy is half of it; the SUPPLY is the other half. This app holds no command string at all, so there is nothing for a banner to concatenate on even if somebody rewrote the sentence.
mutations.note: The second guard of the pair, and the one a check on the COPY alone would not cover: it reddens on the supply coming back, not on the sentence changing. Re-adds `AA.CONFIG.rebuild`, which is what config.js deliberately holds a comment where instead of a key.
mutations.find: // There is deliberately NO `rebuild` entry here. It held the two build
mutations.replace:
rebuild: ["venv-win/Scripts/python.exe scripts/build_topology_projection.py"],
    // There is deliberately NO `rebuild` entry here. It held the two build
mutations.expect_red: this app holds no terminal command for a banner to render

mutations.contract: A card's crop is capped by WIDTH, so the figure the highlight overlay is positioned against stays the picture itself -- a percentage box lands on the cell it names rather than in a letterbox beside it.
mutations.note: The pre-2026-09-15 rule this replaces capped the HEIGHT and let `object-fit: contain` inset the picture inside an element that kept the block's full width. The element then measures ~2.0:1 where the crop is 1.33:1 and every pct() box in views/crop.js points past the picture. Only measurable in a browser, and only on a card that HAS a highlight to mis-place -- which is why the witness lives beside the card-layout block rather than in the fast tier.
mutations.expect_red: the crop's element IS the picture — its box still carries the crop's own aspect ratio, so a percentage lands where it reads

mutations.contract: A balloon crop names TWO images, and the detail pane fetches both: the crop and its parts-list row, awaited together so the second is on screen with the first.

Not witnessable in the fast tier at all: topology_app.js is not in run_tests.cjs's file list.

mutations.contract: The hover card builds its own fetch list and carries the same second image: a balloon crop's card shows the parts-list row, not the missing-image line.

A separate entry from the pane's because `imageCache` is shared -- whichever fetcher reaches a PNG first is the only one that touches the adapter, so the two can only be observed on two different rows and only fail one check each.

mutations.contract: A grid row whose number carries no plus/minus says so, in the reader's own words: VA.edgeAttention raises the `no tolerance recorded` badge on every zero-width edge, one per row.

mutations.contract: A nav click whose worksheet read failed shows the sentence saying so -- never the PREVIOUS node's prose under this node's title. loadWorksheet() only assigns on success, so navFailed has to clear the text.
mutations.note: The second of navigate()'s three stated contracts; only the rejection arm had a witness (nav-click-never-wedges). Measured 2026-09-16 with this line deleted: fast 308/308, node-fs 382/382, browser 20/20 -- entirely silent. It is observable because paint() computes hasWorksheet from `sheet.worksheet_file` (the projection, not the text), so the toggle is still offered and views/worksheet.js then renders the new subject's path over the old subject's body. The witness needs a SUCCESSFUL read first, which this seam's empty `texts` cannot give -- hence the suite's `__WORKSHEET_MARKER__` stand-in.
mutations.suite: no nav click wedges the page
mutations.expect_red: a node whose worksheet read FAILED shows the sentence saying so, never the previous node's prose under this node's title

mutations.contract: A browser suite prints the label the SUITES registry dispatches it under. The key is the label, so a `--only` filter can be copied straight off a failing line and mutation_witnesses.json's `suite` values mean what they say.
mutations.note: mutation_witness_tier_repair single-sourced the labels and left the pass-through unobserved: dropping the argument left every tier green and printed `[undefined] 2/2 sub-checks passed: PASS`. --only filters on the registry key rather than the printed line, so even the mutation tier keeps working -- the damage is silent by construction. The originating issue's runtime check was dismissed as comparing a string to itself; it is not, once the in-body copies are gone.
